events.context: 【BBC Sport】Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Peres Jepchirchir won the 2026 Sydney marathon by three minutes and 40 seconds Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for a doping violation. The 33-year-old, who also won Olympic gold in 2021, was provisionally suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) in October after an out-of-competition sample tested positive for erythropoietin (EPO). The sample was collected in Kenya prior to Jepchirchir winning the Sydney Marathon on 30 August 2026 and returned an adverse finding on 17 September. She is one of three high-profile Kenyan athletes to have been sanctioned. Veronica Loleo has also been banned for three years after admitting using EPO, while Ronald Korir has received a six-year ban after failing to explain abnormalities found in his biological passport. EPO is a natural substance produced within the kidneys that stimulates the creation of new red blood cells. If injected, it increases the amount of red blood cells, which carry oxygen to the muscles, in the blood stream but is only detectable in urine or blood for a short window of time. Jepchirchir's other major wins came at the New York Marathon in 2021, the Boston Marathon in 2022 and the London Marathon in 2024. While she denied using EPO, she signed an admission of violations form and accepted disqualification of all her competitive results since 17 July 2026. "The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go," said Brett Clothier, chief executive of the AIU. "The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country. "We will discuss the details behind these commitments with the Kenyan government in the coming months." In September, Kenya was awarded the right to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, with London and Rome missing out. The decision increased scrutiny of the country's efforts to tackle a long-running doping problem, with more than 140 Kenyan athletes, predominantly distance runners, having been suspended by the AIU since 2017. World football's governing body has confirmed the three candidates for the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress in Morocco on 18 March. European football's governing body Uefa only identified its candidate Diallo fewer than 48 hours before Wednesday's deadline. French Football Federation (FFF) president Diallo, 63, received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee. Japan Football Association honorary president Tashima, 68, announced his intention to stand against Infantino, 56, earlier this month. Tashima is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach. Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega had also said he intended to stand but was not named as a candidate by Fifa on Thursday. A late and surprise choice, Diallo said: "I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative...I'm entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win." But he is not the Frenchman some believe Uefa really wanted, as it tries to remove Infantino in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Senior figures in European football had hoped to persuade Arsene Wenger - Fifa's head of global development - to stand against his own boss. Some felt that only he possessed the credibility to pose a serious threat to Infantino's plans for a fourth term. But after the former Arsenal manager chose not to proceed, Uefa had no choice but to seek an alternative. So just how credible a challenger is Diallo? Does Infantino's position appear unassailable? 【BBC Sport】Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Mata celebrates winning Euro 2012 with Spain Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from playing at the age of 38. Mata, who made 41 international appearances, was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup, and he helped his country win the European Championship two years later when he scored in the 4-0 final victory against Italy. A former Real Madrid youth player, he joined Valencia in 2007 before a move to Chelsea in August 2011 where he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup. Mata moved to Manchester United in January 2014 and helped them claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup prior to his departure in 2022. He went on to have spells at Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. "Football will never leave my life," said Mata. "There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. "I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer." Mata was Chelsea's player of the year in both full seasons he was at Stamford Bridge. He made 82 league appearances for the club, scoring 18 goals. "What a player," Chelsea posted on social media. At Manchester United, he scored 51 goals in 285 outings before leaving after his contract expired. "Congratulations on a fantastic career, Juan!
